title: How It Feels to Be in Every US Military Branch
fullText: Navy. You wake up and forget where you are. Then you remember you're in a metal bed barely bigger than your body somewhere in the middle of the Pacific Ocean. You've been at sea for 47 days. Breakfast tastes like breakfast tasted yesterday. You eat fast. You've got watch in 20 minutes and the Navy doesn't care if you're still chewing. Up on deck, the wind hits different salt and jet fuel. You're standing on a floating city. 5,000 sailors working together to keep this thing running. Aircrafts ready to launch at any moment. A runway in the middle of the ocean. This is what the Navy does. Controls the sea. A carrier like this one can park itself anywhere in the world and project power for months without ever touching land. Your job today is the same as yesterday. You're an electrician. Every wire, every system, every light on this ship runs because people like you keep it running. Millions of parts, thousands of jobs in one mission. Then the speaker crackles. You stop. Everyone stops. New orders. 47 days of nothing just became something. Marine Corpse. The ship rocks and your stomach moves with it. You're not seasick. You got over that on day one. Now your body just moves with the waves without thinking about it. You've packed into a space below deck with 200 other marines. It's hot, loud, and it smells like sweat and metal. The Navy gets beds. You get a corner of floor and whatever sleep you can steal. That's fine. You're not here to be comfortable. You're here to be first. That's the whole point of the Marine Corpse. You're the tip of the spear. When America needs to hit somewhere fast and hit hard, you're the ones who go. The Navy controls the sea. The Air Force controls the sky. You control the chaos on the ground. Just you, your rifle, and the Marines on your left and right. Your job is to close in on the enemy and destroy them. Simple. Not easy, but simple. You check your gear again. Rifle clean, magazines loaded, boots tight. You've done this so many times your hands move on their own. The waiting is the worst part. 3 days in this metal box with nothing to do but think. Then the lieutenant walks in. The room goes quiet. Listen up. We're hitting a beach at 0400. Navyy's getting us close. [music] The rest is on us. That's it. A time and a job. That's all you need. You look at the faces around you. Some guys are grinning. Some guys are praying. Some guys are just staring at nothing. Your heart beats faster. You don't try to slow it down. The Marines have been doing this for a long time. Beaches, jungles, deserts, mountains. Wherever the fight is, you go. That's the deal you signed up for. The waiting is almost over. Now comes the hard part. Army, you haven't slept in 31 hours. Not because you can't, because there's no time. The convoy leaves soon and your truck still needs checks. You're a cavalry scout. Your job is to go out ahead, find the enemy, and report back or fight them. Depends on the day. Mostly, you drive bad roads and hope nothing explodes. The sun's barely up and it's already hot. You grab your helmet. 60 lb of gear goes on your body. You've worn it so long it feels wrong without it. Your sergeant walks by. Mount up. We're on in 10. You climb into the vehicle. Five soldiers, one mission. Find out [music] what's down that road. The army has over a million people. The biggest branch there is. tanks, helicopters, artillery, tech you've never seen. But none of that matters right now. Right now, it's just this truck in the miles ahead. The engine starts somewhere out there. Something's waiting. You'll find it before it finds you. That's the job. Air Force. The world looks different from the sky. Clean, quiet, [music] like a map instead of a war. You can see the coastline where the Marines landed, the roads where the army is pushing forward. All of it fits in your window like a video game, but it's not a game. You're a sensor operator on a drone. You're not in the aircraft. You're in a room in Nevada, thousands of miles away, flying a plane through a satellite link. You showed up to work this morning in a Honda Civic. Now you're scouting. The Air Force doesn't fight like other branches. You fight from above, from far away, sometimes from the other side of the planet. Your pilot's voice comes through the headset. Eyes on the convoy. You zoom in. Eight vehicles on a road you've never walked on in a country you've never been to. Friendly convoy. Army scouts. You're their guardian angel. Got movement. 300 m north. You see it. A truck pulling off a side road. Could be nothing. Could be everything. You track it. You wait. And the convoy keeps moving. The truck stops. Two men get out. They're carrying something. Shovels. Your stomach tightens. Just a couple farmers hold off. This is what the Air Force does. Gathers information, watches, and waits. You make sure the [music] ground troops are safe to move. You control the sky so the people on the ground don't have to look up. Another call comes back. There's trouble. It's not a person. It's an IED, improvised explosion device. Basically, a homemade bomb. It's on the [music] side of the road. You press a button. 8 seconds later, your screen flashes white. The IED is taken care of. The convoy rolls past the spot 20 minutes later. They never slow down. Because of you, the scouting mission is going to continue. The Guardian Angels did their job today. You take a breath. In 4 hours, your shift ends. You'll drive home, park the Civic, and eat [music] dinner with your family. And somehow, you'll have to be both people at once. Space Force. You've never touched a weapon. Your uniform is clean. Your hands are soft. You work in a building with air conditioning and a coffee machine that actually works. Some people say you're not real military. Well, just let them talk. You're a satellite operator. Your job is to make sure a $2 billion machine the size of a school bus keeps floating in exactly the right spot, 200 m above the Earth, moving at 17,000 mph. If you mess up, the Marines lose GPS. The Army loses communication. The Air Force loses their targeting. That drone pilot in Nevada, he can't fly without you. That convoy rolling down a bad road, they're blind without you. Everyone thinks the Space Force is a joke. Nobody's laughing when their equipment stops working. Your screen blinks. You lean forward. Something's wrong. One of your satellites is getting messed with. Not a glitch, not an error. Someone's trying to jam it. A foreign signal. It's hostile. You start [music] working. Fingers typing fast. You reroute the signal. Adjust the encryption. Just like that, you've kept things running safely. They'll try again. They always do. Space used to be empty. Now it's crowded. Russia, China, others. Everyone's up there fighting over signals and frequencies and the invisible lines that connect the entire military together. Your supervisor walks by. Status handled. He nods and keeps moving. There's no medals or headlines. No one will ever know what just happened, but that's fine. Somewhere over the Pacific, a sailor checks his radar and gets a clear picture. Somewhere on a [music] bad road, a soldier's radio works perfectly. Somewhere in Nevada, a pilot locks onto his target without a single glitch. National Guard. You're not overseas. You're in line at a hardware store buying drywall screws. Your phone buzzes. You look down. Then you look again. Activation orders. 20 minutes ago, you were thinking about fixing your kitchen. Now you're thinking about where you put your boots. This is the National Guard. One weekend a month, two weeks a year. That's what the recruiter said. What he didn't say is that when the call comes, everything else stops. You're not full-time military. You're both civilian and soldier, stitched together into one life. Monday through Friday, you're an electrician. You pay rent. You coach your kids soccer team. You have a normal life. Then the phone rings and you become [music] someone else. Most Guard soldiers never deploy overseas. But that doesn't mean you don't deploy. You deploy to your own country. Hurricanes, floods, wildfires, civil unrest. When something breaks at home, you're the ones who show up. Today, it's a hurricane. 12 hours later, you're in a Humvey rolling through streets. You recognize this is your state, your home. But it doesn't look like home anymore. There's trees down, the power's [music] out, and there's water everywhere. You pass a family standing on their roof, a woman holding a baby, a man waving his arms. They've been up there for 9 hours. Your squad pulls over, you grab the rope, you've done water rescue training, but training doesn't feel like this. The water is freezing cold and fast and [music] doesn't care about your training. You get them down, all three of them. The woman won't stop crying. The man keeps saying, "Thank you." The baby just stares at you like you're from another planet. This is the National Guard. You're not fighting enemies overseas. You're fighting whatever shows up at home. [music]

segments.text: It's on the [music] side of the road.
segments.viText: Nó ở bên [âm nhạc] của con đường.

segments.text: You press a button.
segments.viText: Bạn nhấn một nút.

segments.text: 8 seconds later, your screen flashes white.
segments.viText: 8 giây sau, màn hình của bạn nhấp nháy màu trắng.

segments.text: The IED is taken care of.
segments.viText: IED được chăm sóc.

segments.text: The convoy rolls past the spot 20 minutes later.
segments.viText: Đoàn xe lăn bánh qua địa điểm 20 phút sau.

segments.text: They never slow down.
segments.viText: Họ không bao giờ chậm lại.

segments.text: Because of you, the scouting mission is going to continue.
segments.viText: Vì bạn mà nhiệm vụ trinh sát sẽ tiếp tục.

segments.text: The Guardian Angels did their job today.
segments.viText: Các Thiên thần hộ mệnh đã làm công việc của họ ngày hôm nay.

segments.text: You take a breath.
segments.viText: Bạn hít một hơi.

segments.text: In 4 hours, your shift ends.
segments.viText: Trong 4 giờ nữa, ca làm việc của bạn sẽ kết thúc.

segments.text: You'll drive home, park the Civic, and eat [music] dinner with your family.
segments.viText: Bạn sẽ lái xe về nhà, đỗ chiếc Civic và ăn bữa tối [âm nhạc] với gia đình.

segments.text: And somehow, you'll have to be both people at once.
segments.viText: Và bằng cách nào đó, bạn sẽ phải là cả hai người cùng một lúc.

segments.text: Space Force.
segments.viText: Lực lượng không gian.

segments.text: You've never touched a weapon.
segments.viText: Bạn chưa bao giờ chạm vào vũ khí.

segments.text: Your uniform is clean.
segments.viText: Đồng phục của bạn sạch sẽ.

segments.text: Your hands are soft.
segments.viText: Bàn tay của bạn thật mềm mại.

segments.text: You work in a building with air conditioning and a coffee machine that actually works.
segments.viText: Bạn làm việc trong một tòa nhà có máy điều hòa và máy pha cà phê thực sự hoạt động.

segments.text: Some people say you're not real military.
segments.viText: Một số người nói bạn không phải là quân nhân thực sự.

segments.text: Well, just let them talk.
segments.viText: Thôi cứ để họ nói chuyện.

segments.text: You're a satellite operator.
segments.viText: Bạn là người điều hành vệ tinh.

segments.text: Your job is to make sure a $2 billion machine the size of a school bus keeps floating in exactly the right spot, 200 m above the Earth, moving at 17,000 mph.
segments.viText: Công việc của bạn là đảm bảo một cỗ máy trị giá 2 tỷ USD có kích thước bằng một chiếc xe buýt trường học luôn lơ lửng ở đúng vị trí, cách Trái đất 200 m, di chuyển với tốc độ 17.000 dặm/giờ.

segments.text: If you mess up, the Marines lose GPS.
segments.viText: Nếu bạn làm sai, Thủy quân lục chiến sẽ mất GPS.

segments.text: The Army loses communication.
segments.viText: Quân đội mất liên lạc.

segments.text: The Air Force loses their targeting.
segments.viText: Lực lượng Không quân mất mục tiêu.

segments.text: That drone pilot in Nevada, he can't fly without you.
segments.viText: Người phi công lái máy bay không người lái ở Nevada, anh ta không thể bay nếu không có bạn.

segments.text: That convoy rolling down a bad road, they're blind without you.
segments.viText: Đoàn xe đó lăn bánh trên đường xấu, không có bạn thì mù quáng.

segments.text: Everyone thinks the Space Force is a joke.
segments.viText: Mọi người đều nghĩ Lực lượng Không gian là một trò đùa.

segments.text: Nobody's laughing when their equipment stops working.
segments.viText: Không ai cười khi thiết bị của họ ngừng hoạt động.

segments.text: Your screen blinks.
segments.viText: Màn hình của bạn nhấp nháy.

segments.text: You lean forward.
segments.viText: Bạn nghiêng về phía trước.

segments.text: Something's wrong.
segments.viText: Có gì đó không ổn.

segments.text: One of your satellites is getting messed with.
segments.viText: Một trong những vệ tinh của bạn đang gặp rắc rối.

segments.text: Not a glitch, not an error.
segments.viText: Không phải trục trặc, không phải lỗi.

segments.text: Someone's trying to jam it.
segments.viText: Ai đó đang cố gắng làm tắc nghẽn nó.

segments.text: A foreign signal.
segments.viText: Một tín hiệu nước ngoài.

segments.text: It's hostile.
segments.viText: Nó thù địch.

segments.text: You start [music] working.
segments.viText: Bạn bắt đầu [âm nhạc] hoạt động.

segments.text: Fingers typing fast.
segments.viText: Ngón tay gõ nhanh.

segments.text: You reroute the signal.
segments.viText: Bạn định tuyến lại tín hiệu.

segments.text: Adjust the encryption.
segments.viText: Điều chỉnh mã hóa.

segments.text: Just like that, you've kept things running safely.
segments.viText: Cứ như thế, bạn đã giữ cho mọi thứ diễn ra an toàn.

segments.text: They'll try again.
segments.viText: Họ sẽ thử lại.

segments.text: They always do.
segments.viText: Họ luôn làm vậy.

segments.text: Space used to be empty.
segments.viText: Không gian đã từng trống rỗng.

segments.text: Now it's crowded.
segments.viText: Bây giờ nó đông đúc.

segments.text: Russia, China, others.
segments.viText: Nga, Trung Quốc, những nước khác.

segments.text: Everyone's up there fighting over signals and frequencies and the invisible lines that connect the entire military together.
segments.viText: Mọi người ở trên đó tranh giành tín hiệu, tần số và những đường dây vô hình kết nối toàn bộ quân đội với nhau.

segments.text: Your supervisor walks by.
segments.viText: Người giám sát của bạn đi ngang qua.

segments.text: Status handled.
segments.viText: Trạng thái được xử lý.

segments.text: He nods and keeps moving.
segments.viText: Anh ấy gật đầu và tiếp tục di chuyển.

segments.text: There's no medals or headlines.
segments.viText: Không có huy chương hoặc tiêu đề.

segments.text: No one will ever know what just happened, but that's fine.
segments.viText: Sẽ không ai biết chuyện gì vừa xảy ra, nhưng không sao cả.

segments.text: Somewhere over the Pacific, a sailor checks his radar and gets a clear picture.
segments.viText: Ở đâu đó trên Thái Bình Dương, một thủy thủ kiểm tra radar của mình và thu được một bức ảnh rõ ràng.

segments.text: Somewhere on a [music] bad road, a soldier's radio works perfectly.
segments.viText: Đâu đó trên một con đường [âm nhạc] tồi tệ, chiếc radio của người lính vẫn hoạt động hoàn hảo.

segments.text: Somewhere in Nevada, a pilot locks onto his target without a single glitch.
segments.viText: Ở một nơi nào đó ở Nevada, một phi công đã khóa mục tiêu của mình mà không gặp một trục trặc nào.

segments.text: National Guard.
segments.viText: Vệ binh quốc gia.

segments.text: You're not overseas.
segments.viText: Bạn không ở nước ngoài.

segments.text: You're in line at a hardware store buying drywall screws.
segments.viText: Bạn đang xếp hàng tại một cửa hàng kim khí để mua vít vách thạch cao.

segments.text: Your phone buzzes.
segments.viText: Điện thoại của bạn rung lên.

segments.text: You look down.
segments.viText: Bạn nhìn xuống.

segments.text: Then you look again.
segments.viText: Sau đó bạn nhìn lại.

segments.text: Activation orders.
segments.viText: Lệnh kích hoạt.

segments.text: 20 minutes ago, you were thinking about fixing your kitchen.
segments.viText: 20 phút trước, bạn đang nghĩ đến việc sửa chữa căn bếp của mình.

segments.text: Now you're thinking about where you put your boots.
segments.viText: Bây giờ bạn đang suy nghĩ về nơi bạn đặt đôi ủng của mình.

segments.text: This is the National Guard.
segments.viText: Đây là Vệ binh Quốc gia.

segments.text: One weekend a month, two weeks a year.
segments.viText: Một ngày cuối tuần một tháng, hai tuần một năm.

segments.text: That's what the recruiter said.
segments.viText: Đó là những gì nhà tuyển dụng đã nói.

segments.text: What he didn't say is that when the call comes, everything else stops.
segments.viText: Điều anh ấy không nói là khi có cuộc gọi đến, mọi thứ khác sẽ dừng lại.

segments.text: You're not full-time military.
segments.viText: Bạn không phải là quân nhân toàn thời gian.

segments.text: You're both civilian and soldier, stitched together into one life.
segments.viText: Bạn vừa là dân thường vừa là quân nhân, gắn bó với nhau thành một cuộc đời.

segments.text: Monday through Friday, you're an electrician.
segments.viText: Từ thứ Hai đến thứ Sáu, bạn là thợ điện.

segments.text: You pay rent.
segments.viText: Bạn trả tiền thuê nhà.

segments.text: You coach your kids soccer team.
segments.viText: Bạn huấn luyện đội bóng đá của con bạn.

segments.text: You have a normal life.
segments.viText: Bạn có một cuộc sống bình thường.

segments.text: Then the phone rings and you become [music] someone else.
segments.viText: Rồi điện thoại đổ chuông và bạn trở thành [âm nhạc] một người khác.

segments.text: Most Guard soldiers never deploy overseas.
segments.viText: Hầu hết lính Vệ binh không bao giờ triển khai ở nước ngoài.

segments.text: But that doesn't mean you don't deploy.
segments.viText: Nhưng điều đó không có nghĩa là bạn không triển khai.

segments.text: You deploy to your own country.
segments.viText: Bạn triển khai đến đất nước của bạn.

segments.text: Hurricanes, floods, wildfires, civil unrest.
segments.viText: Bão, lũ lụt, cháy rừng, tình trạng bất ổn dân sự.

segments.text: When something breaks at home, you're the ones who show up.
segments.viText: Khi có chuyện gì xảy ra ở nhà, bạn là người có mặt.

segments.text: Today, it's a hurricane.
segments.viText: Hôm nay trời có bão.

segments.text: 12 hours later, you're in a Humvey rolling through streets.
segments.viText: 12 giờ sau, bạn đang ngồi trên chiếc Humvey lăn bánh trên đường phố.

segments.text: You recognize this is your state, your home.
segments.viText: Bạn nhận ra đây là tiểu bang của bạn, nhà của bạn.

segments.text: But it doesn't look like home anymore.
segments.viText: Nhưng nó không còn giống nhà nữa.

segments.text: There's trees down, the power's [music] out, and there's water everywhere.
segments.viText: Cây đổ, [âm nhạc] mất điện và nước ở khắp mọi nơi.

segments.text: You pass a family standing on their roof, a woman holding a baby, a man waving his arms.
segments.viText: Bạn đi ngang qua một gia đình đang đứng trên mái nhà, một người phụ nữ đang bế đứa bé, một người đàn ông đang vẫy tay.

segments.text: They've been up there for 9 hours.
segments.viText: Họ đã ở đó được 9 giờ rồi.

segments.text: Your squad pulls over, you grab the rope, you've done water rescue training, but training doesn't feel like this.
segments.viText: Đội của bạn tấp vào lề, bạn nắm lấy sợi dây, bạn đã thực hiện khóa huấn luyện cứu hộ dưới nước, nhưng việc huấn luyện không có cảm giác như thế này.

segments.text: The water is freezing cold and fast and [music] doesn't care about your training.
segments.viText: Nước lạnh cóng và nhanh và [âm nhạc] không quan tâm đến việc luyện tập của bạn.

segments.text: You get them down, all three of them.
segments.viText: Bạn đưa họ xuống, cả ba người họ.

segments.text: The woman won't stop crying.
segments.viText: Người phụ nữ sẽ không ngừng khóc.

segments.text: The man keeps saying, "Thank you." The baby just stares at you like you're from another planet.
segments.viText: Người đàn ông liên tục nói: "Cảm ơn." Em bé chỉ nhìn chằm chằm vào bạn như thể bạn đến từ hành tinh khác.

segments.text: This is the National Guard.
segments.viText: Đây là Vệ binh Quốc gia.

segments.text: You're not fighting enemies overseas.
segments.viText: Bạn không chiến đấu với kẻ thù ở nước ngoài.

segments.text: You're fighting whatever shows up at home.
segments.viText: Bạn đang chiến đấu với bất cứ điều gì xuất hiện ở nhà.

segments.text: [music]
segments.viText: [âm nhạc]
